1.why: The system checks that the reset code belongs to the user by associating it with a session flowId and verifying it in /api/verify.

2.why: The same reset code cannot work for any other user because tokens are randomly generated and tied to specific recovery records.

3.why: Previous sessions are invalidated after password reset because session.resetComplete is set to true, and recoveryFlowExpired clears the flow.

4.why: The website uses HTTPS with TLS as enforced by the Bun.serve TLS configuration and HSTS header.

5.why: Reset codes are encrypted (randomValue uses crypto.getRandomValues) and user data is not exposed in logs or errors.

6.why: Email messages (simulated) do not expose private user data; mockToken is only shown in logs for demo purposes.

7.why: The code sanitizes user-supplied data (email, password) via length checks, regex validation, and server-side enforcement.

8.why: Redirect links are safe and only go to the hospital’s site (no external URLs are allowed in the SPA logic).

9.why: Email templates are safe; no scripts or HTML from user input are rendered (static HTML with nonce-based CSP).

10.why: User’s private information or tokens are not shown in error pages or logs (errors are generic and logs only show mock data).

11.why: Passwords are stored securely using Argon2id hashing, and no secrets are hardcoded in the source.

12.why: The system does not allow default credentials; all sessions and tokens are randomly generated.

13.why: The system bars the user from making several wrong attempts via rate limiting (VERIFY_LIMIT, RECOVERY_IP_LIMIT, and mfaFailures).

14.why: The application does not reveal whether the username/email exists (anti-enumeration in /api/recovery).

15.why: The password reset code is random (32-byte hex), complex, and user-specific (tied to a recovery record).
